'''Laurence Frederick Abbott'''<ref name=CV>[https://sni-db.stanford.edu/cv/VitaLFA.pdf "LAURENCE F. ABBOTT CV"]. Retrieved on 31 March 2020.</ref> (born 1950) is an American theoretical neuroscientist, who is currently the William Bloor Professor of Theoretical Neuroscience at [[Columbia University]], where he helped create the Center for Theoretical Neuroscience. He is widely regarded as one of the leaders of [[theoretical neuroscience]], and is coauthor, along with [[Peter Dayan]], on the first comprehensive textbook on theoretical neuroscience, which is considered to be the standard text for students and researchers entering theoretical neuroscience.<ref>Plunkett, John. [https://mitpress.mit.edu/books/theoretical-neuroscience "Theoretical Neuroscience"], ''[[MIT Press]]'', Retrieved on 31 March 2020.</ref> He helped invent the dynamic clamp method alongside [[Eve Marder]].<ref name="MyUser_Symmetrymagazine.org_May_12_2015c">{{cite web |url=http://www.symmetrymagazine.org/article/july-2014/a-physicist-in-the-neurobiology-lab |title=A physicist in the neurobiology lab |newspaper=Symmetrymagazine.org |date=  8 July 2014|author= |access-date= May 12, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140713064723/http://www.symmetrymagazine.org/article/july-2014/a-physicist-in-the-neurobiology-lab |archive-date=13 July 2014}}</ref>

Abbott has received numerous awards for his work in the field, including memberships in the [[National Academy of Sciences]] and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]. In 2010, he received the [[Swartz Prize for Theoretical and Computational Neuroscience]]. In 2022 he was awarded the [[Gruber Neuroscience Prize]].<ref>[https://gruber.yale.edu/neuroscience Gruber Neuroscience Prize 2022]</ref> In 2024, he was awarded [[The Brain Prize]] for contributions to theoretical neuroscience, alongside [[Terrence Sejnowski]]  and [[Haim Sompolinsky]].<ref>Columbia | Zuckerman Institute. (2024, March 6). [https://zuckermaninstitute.columbia.edu/scientist-columbia-s-zuckerman-institute-wins-prestigious-brain-prize Scientist at Columbia's Zuckerman Institute wins prestigious brain prize.]</ref>

==Biography==
Abbott attended [[Oberlin College]] from 1968 to 1971, where he received a bachelor's degree in physics.<ref name= CV /> He subsequently attended graduate school at [[Brandeis University]] from 1973 to 1977, where he received his Ph.D. in physics. 
==Scientific career==
He subsequently worked in theoretical [[particle physics]], serving as research associate at [[Stanford Linear Accelerator Center]] from 1977 to 1979, as a Scientific Associate at the Theory division at [[CERN]] from 1980 to 1981, and as a tenure track professor in the physics department at Brandeis from 1979 to 2005.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=|first=|date=5 October 2016|title=Larry Abbott|url=|journal=Neuron|volume=92|issue=1|pages=9–10|doi=10.1016/j.neuron.2016.09.041|doi-access=free}}</ref> Abbott began his transition to neuroscience research in 1989, joined the Department of Biology at Brandeis in 1993, and was the co-director of Brandeis Sloan Center for Theoretical Neurobiology from 1994 to 2002, the director of the Volen National Center for Complex Systems at Brandeis from 1997 to 2002, and a visiting faculty at [[UCSF]] Sloan Center for Theoretical Neuroscience from 1994 to 2002.<ref name= CV /> At Brandeis, he held the position of the Nancy Lurie Marks Professor of Neuroscience from 1997 to 2002 and the Zalman Abraham Kekst Professor of Neuroscience from 2003 to 2005.<ref name=Columbia-University-Presidential-Scholar /> In 2005, he joined the faculty of [[Columbia University]], where he is currently a member of the Department of Neuroscience, and the Department of Physiology and Cellular Biophysics. He is co-director of the Center for Theoretical Neuroscience.<ref name="Larry Abbott, PhD">{{Cite web|url= https://neuroscience.columbia.edu/profile/larryabbott |title= Larry Abbott, PhD|access-date= Jan 22, 2020 |website= Columbia.edu}}</ref><ref name="MyUser_The_New_York_Times_May_12_2015c">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/11/11/science/learning-how-little-we-know-about-the-brain.html |title=Learning How Little We Know About the Brain |newspaper=The New York Times |date= November 10, 2014 |author= |access-date= May 12, 2015}}</ref> He has been a senior fellow at HHMI [[Janelia Farm Research Campus]] since 2015.<ref name= CV /><ref name=Columbia-University-Presidential-Scholar />
